## Browse by model

**${main_count} source-linked cases** in six families. Each table introduces three different subjects, with a preview entry, introduction, model label, creator, and source. Media without verified publication permission opens at its original source; it is not an embedded preview. All versions and records remain in the [full catalog](docs/catalog.en.md). This is editorial navigation, not a model ranking.

Version order is editorial: important current source-labeled versions first, then source dates within a version. Comparable popularity data is not yet available. [Ordering policy](docs/discovery-order.md).

<a id="how-to-use"></a>
## Start here

1. **Find an idea.** Browse a model family below, or search the gallery by title, creator, and model.
2. **Check the evidence.** Open a case for the original post, author, method, and prompt status: published, partial, or unpublished.
3. **Plan your own attempt.** Use the documented method as a starting point. Access, settings, and results may differ; this archive does not reproduce or certify model outputs.

No account, API key, or install is needed to browse. Model names are source claims. **Code licensing does not grant rights to third-party media or prompts.**

[Models](#showcase) · [Recent posts](#latest) · [Types](#by-type) · [Contribute](#contribute) · [Rights & languages](#rights)

<a id="contribute"></a>
## Contribute a case or correction

[Submit a case](https://github.com/jammyfu/awesome-ai-model-showcases/issues/new?template=case-submission.yml) with its original author, source URL, published prompt or “unpublished,” and model or method evidence. No coding required. Attribution, broken-link, and translation corrections are welcome.

For a pull request, follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Edit source inventories or the four templates, regenerate, review, and run the single [verification entry point](tools/verify.py).

<a id="local-setup"></a>
<details>
<summary>Run the gallery locally</summary>

Browsing the existing static gallery only needs Python 3:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jammyfu/awesome-ai-model-showcases.git
cd awesome-ai-model-showcases
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory docs
```

Open [localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000/?lang=en). For public hosting, use the [approved-media build](MEDIA_RIGHTS.md#publication-and-playback-checks), not the raw archive directory. Development checks additionally need the dependencies in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

</details>

<a id="rights"></a>
<a id="faq"></a>
## Rights, scope, and languages

- **Scope:** inventory updated **${inventory_date}**; **${pending_count} pending cases** are outside the **${main_count}** homepage total. GIF subproject, remakes, failures, and repository seeds stay separate.
- **Media:** **${media_count} existing catalog cases have approved local media**. The two Claude spotlight frames above have their own documented grant; other catalog records link to the source. Public access, attribution, or download does not establish reuse rights.
- **License:** [MIT](LICENSE) covers source code and original project documentation, not third-party media, prompts, trademarks, or likenesses. Read [MEDIA_RIGHTS.md](MEDIA_RIGHTS.md). Rights holders may [request correction or removal](https://github.com/jammyfu/awesome-ai-model-showcases/issues/new).
- **Languages:** the README and case evidence support English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, and 日本語. AI translations are **not human-reviewed**; originals remain available. The gallery interface supports **English / 简体中文 only**. [Translation policy and coverage](docs/translation-policy.md).

Want to reuse this documentation structure? Start with the [README pattern and checks](docs/readme-pattern.md), and replace every project-specific claim with evidence from your own repository.
